content: Patients with a history of severe allergic reactions, such as anaphylaxis, to any known components of the product should not use it. If persistent diarrhea occurs—defined as three or more loose bowel movements within a 24-hour period for two consecutive days—following product administration, patients must notify their physician. Patients should also be instructed not to take any oral antibiotic therapy for up to eight weeks after product administration unless explicitly directed by their physician. The product is not systemically absorbed following rectal administration, and maternal use is not expected to result in fetal exposure. Similarly, systemic absorption by the mother after rectal administration is not anticipated to expose a breastfeeding child. The product is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. This microbiota-based live biotherapeutic is delivered rectally to introduce a broad consortium of diverse microbes into the gut, aiming to reduce recurrent Clostridioides difficile infections after antibiotic treatment. However, the exact mechanism of action has not been established. Before use, the product must be completely thawed by placing the carton in a refrigerator at 2–8°C (36–46°F) for approximately 24 hours. It should not be refrozen after thawing. The thawed carton can be stored in the refrigerator at 2–8°C (36–46°F) and must be used within five days, including the thawing time. Thawing should not be done using a heat source, such as a microwave or hot water. Condensation after thawing is normal. To prepare for administration, remove the thawed carton from the refrigerator. Then, take the bag containing the thawed microbiota out of the outer carton and the inner carton insert. Do not remove the bag containing the thawed microbiota from the sealed outer bag. Locate the administration set (provided), a water-soluble lubricant (not included), and a disposable underpad (not included). Refer to the prescribing information for detailed instructions on setting up the bag for administration. This product is for rectal administration only. Prepare the patient for administration by asking them to empty their bladder and bowel, if possible. Position the patient in the left-side position or the knee-chest position for rectal administration. Apply a water-soluble lubricant to the tip of the administration tube, and gently insert the tube approximately 12 cm (5 inches) into the rectum, angling slightly toward the umbilicus. Hold the administration tube in place with one hand throughout the procedure to maintain its position in the rectum. With the other hand, open the pinch clamp on the administration tube and gradually raise the bag to allow delivery via gravity flow. Ensure the administration tube does not sag or loop, as this will prevent the entire dose from being delivered. Do not squeeze the bag, as this may cause patient discomfort. Do not hang the bag from an IV stand. Once the entire dose has been delivered, close the pinch clamp and slowly withdraw the tube, taking care to prevent any residual suspension remaining in the tube from leaking out (some suspension will remain in the tube after administration). After the dose has been delivered, keep the patient in the same position for up to 15 minutes to minimize any cramping that may occur. Dispose of all components used for administration in medical waste. The product contains live microorganisms, so it is essential to follow storage requirements carefully.
